questions.text:
किसी वैद्युत-रासायनिक सेल में निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया होती है :
2Cu+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Cu(s) + Zn2+(aq)
E°सेल = 1.28 V
जैसे-जैसे अभिक्रिया आगे बढ़ती है, सेल के समग्र विभव का क्या होगा ?
questions.text_english:
In an electrochemical cell, the following reaction takes place :
2Cu+(aq) + Zn(s) → 2Cu(s) + Zn2+(aq)
E°cell = 1.28 V
As the reaction progresses, what will happen to the overall voltage of the cell?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). According to the Nernst equation, Ecell = E°cell - (RT/nF) ln Q. As the reaction progresses, Zn is oxidised and Zn2+ accumulates, while Cu+ is consumed. The reaction quotient Q = [Zn2+]/[Cu+]2 increases as [Zn2+] increases and [Cu+] decreases. An increase in Q means ln Q increases, so the cell voltage decreases. Option (A) is wrong because voltage changes as concentrations change. Option (C) is wrong because [Cu+] decreases (it is being consumed), not increases. Option (D) is wrong because an increase in [Zn2+] increases Q and therefore decreases, not increases, the cell voltage.

questions.text:
Fe3+, Sc3+, Cr3+ और Co3+ आयनों में से जलीय विलयन में कौन-सा रंगहीन है?
[परमाणु क्रमांक : Fe = 26, Sc = 21, Cr = 24, Co = 27]
questions.text_english:
Out of Fe3+, Sc3+, Cr3+ and Co3+ ions, the one which is colourless in aqueous solution is :
[Atomic number : Fe = 26, Sc = 21, Cr = 24, Co = 27]
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Sc3+. The colour of transition metal ions in solution arises from d-d electronic transitions. For such transitions to occur, the ion must have partially filled d-orbitals. Sc (Z=21) has the electronic configuration [Ar] 3d1 4s2, so Sc3+ has the configuration [Ar] with completely empty 3d orbitals (3d0). Since there are no d-electrons to undergo d-d transitions, Sc3+ is colourless in aqueous solution. Fe3+ (3d5), Cr3+ (3d3), and Co3+ (3d6) all have partially filled d-orbitals and therefore show colour due to d-d transitions.

questions.text: हॉफमान ब्रोमामाइड निम्नीकरण अभिक्रिया निम्नलिखित में से किसके द्वारा दी जाती है?
questions.text_english: Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction is given by :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) ArCONH2. The Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction involves the treatment of a primary amide (RCONH2) with bromine in the presence of aqueous or ethanolic KOH to give a primary amine with one carbon less than the original amide. ArCONH2 is an aromatic primary amide (benzamide type), and when treated with Br2/KOH it gives ArNH2 (aniline type). Option (A) ArNO2 is a nitro compound, (B) ArNH2 is the product, not the starting material, and (D) ArCH2NH2 is a benzylamine, none of which are amides that undergo this reaction.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कार्बोहाइड्रेट की हॉवर्थ संरचना में विभिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं को संख्यांकित किया गया है। ऐनोमरी कार्बन को किस संख्या से संख्यांकित किया गया है?
questions.text_english: In the Haworth structure of the following carbohydrate, various carbon atoms have been numbered. The anomeric carbon is numbered as :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1. The anomeric carbon is the carbon that was the carbonyl carbon (aldehyde or ketone) in the open-chain form and becomes a new chiral centre when the sugar cyclises to form the hemiacetal ring. In glucose, C1 was the aldehyde carbon; upon ring closure it becomes the anomeric carbon, bearing two oxygen substituents — the ring oxygen and the newly formed OH group. This C1 can give rise to the alpha and beta anomers. Carbon 2, 3, 4 are regular chiral centres and C5 is the carbon bearing the CH2OH group.

questions.text: हेनरी स्थिरांक KH का मान होता है :
questions.text_english: The value of Henry's constant KH is :

options.A: उच्चतर विलेयता वाली गैसों के लिए बृहत्तर
options.B: निम्नतर विलेयता वाली गैसों के लिए बृहत्तर
options.D: गैसों की विलेयता से संबंधित नहीं है

options_english.A: greater for gases with higher solubility
options_english.B: greater for gases with lower solubility
options_english.D: not related to the solubility of gases

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B). According to Henry's law, the partial pressure of a gas above a solution is proportional to its mole fraction in the solution: p = KH x. Therefore KH = p/x. A gas with lower solubility has a smaller mole fraction (x) dissolved at a given partial pressure, which means KH = p/x will be larger. Conversely, a highly soluble gas has a larger mole fraction at the same pressure, giving a smaller KH. Option (A) is wrong because higher solubility gives a smaller KH. Options (C) and (D) are incorrect as KH varies from gas to gas and is directly inversely related to solubility.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कथनों में से ग़लत कथन है :
questions.text_english: Out of the following statements, the incorrect statement is :

options.A: La वास्तव में संक्रमण श्रेणी का तत्व है।
options.B: लैंथेनॉयड आकुंचन के कारण Zr और Hf की लगभग समान परमाणु त्रिज्याएं होती हैं।
options.C: La3+ से Lu3+ आयन तक आयनिक त्रिज्या घटती है।
options.D: लैंथेनॉयड रेडियोसक्रिय प्रकृति के होते हैं।

options_english.A: La is actually an element of transition series.
options_english.B: Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii because of lanthanoid contraction.
options_english.C: Ionic radius decreases from La3+ to Lu3+ ion.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). Lanthanoids are NOT radioactive in nature as a general rule; most of them are stable elements. It is the actinoids that are radioactive in nature. Statement (A) is correct — La (Z=57) does not have a 4f electron; its configuration is [Xe]5d16s2, so it is indeed a d-block (transition) element. Statement (B) is correct — due to lanthanoid contraction, Zr (Period 4) and Hf (Period 6) have nearly identical atomic radii (~160 pm), making them very difficult to separate. Statement (C) is correct — ionic radius decreases steadily from La3+ (106 pm) to Lu3+ (85 pm) due to the poor shielding by 4f electrons, which is the lanthanoid contraction.

questions.text: 2-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन, 1-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन, 2-ब्रोमोप्रोपेन और 1-ब्रोमोप्रोपेन में से कौन-सा अणु किरेल प्रकृति का है?
questions.text_english: Out of 2-Bromobutane, 1-Bromobutane, 2-Bromopropane and 1-Bromopropane, the molecule which is chiral in nature is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 2-Bromobutane. A molecule is chiral if it has a carbon atom bearing four different groups (chiral centre/asymmetric carbon). In 2-bromobutane (CH3CHBrCH2CH3), C2 bears H, Br, CH3, and CH2CH3 — four different groups — making it a chiral centre. In 1-bromobutane (BrCH2CH2CH2CH3) and 1-bromopropane (BrCH2CH2CH3), the carbon bearing Br has two H atoms, so no chiral centre. In 2-bromopropane (CH3CHBrCH3), C2 bears H, Br, CH3, and CH3 — two identical methyl groups — so it also has no chiral centre and possesses a plane of symmetry.

questions.text:
नीचे दी गई अभिक्रिया अनुक्रम में, Y की संरचना होगी :
Aniline → (NaNO2/HCl, 0–5°C) → X → (C2H5OH) → Y
questions.text_english:
In the given reaction sequence, the structure of Y would be :
Aniline (C6H5NH2) → (NaNO2/HCl, 0-5°C) → X → (C2H5OH) → Y
questions.image_description: Reaction sequence: Aniline treated with NaNO2/HCl at 0-5°C gives X (benzenediazonium chloride), which is then treated with C2H5OH to give Y. Four structural options are shown: (A) phenol with OH group, (B) benzene ring, (C) nitrobenzene with NO2 group, (D) benzenediazonium chloride salt.
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Benzene. In the first step, aniline reacts with NaNO2 and HCl at 0–5°C to give benzenediazonium chloride (X), C6H5N2+Cl–. This is a diazotisation reaction. In the second step, benzenediazonium chloride is treated with ethanol (C2H5OH), which acts as a mild reducing agent. Ethanol reduces the diazonium salt and the diazonium group (–N2+) is replaced by hydrogen, giving benzene (Y) and liberating N2 gas. The ethanol itself is oxidised to acetaldehyde. Hence Y is benzene, not phenol (which forms on treatment with warm water), not nitrobenzene, and not the diazonium salt itself.

questions.text: क्षारीय माध्यम में MnO4– द्वारा I– के ऑक्सीकरण का उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: The product of the oxidation of I– with MnO4– in alkaline medium is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) IO3–. When iodide ion (I–, oxidation state –1) is oxidised by permanganate (MnO4–) in alkaline medium, the strongly oxidising permanganate converts I– all the way to iodate (IO3–), in which iodine has oxidation state +5. In neutral or acidic medium, the product would be I2, but in alkaline medium the oxidation goes further to give IO3–. The permanganate itself is reduced to MnO2 (oxidation state +4) in alkaline medium. IO4– would require even stronger oxidising conditions and IO– is the hypoiodite formed under milder conditions.

questions.text: पॉलिहैलोजन यौगिकों का उद्योगों और कृषि में व्यापक अनुप्रयोग है। DDT भी एक अत्यंत महत्त्वपूर्ण पॉलिहैलोजन यौगिक है। यह है एक :
questions.text_english: Polyhalogen compounds have wide application in industries and agriculture. DDT is also a very important polyhalogen compound. It is a :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) non-biodegradable insecticide. DDT (dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is a polyhalogen compound that was widely used as an insecticide, especially against mosquitoes. It is highly stable chemically and biologically, meaning it cannot be broken down by microorganisms in the environment. This makes it a non-biodegradable insecticide. Due to this persistent nature, DDT accumulates in the food chain (biomagnification) and causes environmental pollution. It is not a greenhouse gas, not a fertilizer, and its non-biodegradable nature is precisely why its use has been banned in many countries.

questions.text: MnO4– के 1 मोल को Mn2+ में अपचयित करने के लिए कितने विद्युत आवेश की आवश्यकता होगी?
questions.text_english: What amount of electric charge is required for the reduction of 1 mole of MnO4– into Mn2+?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 5F. In MnO4–, manganese has oxidation state +7. In Mn2+, manganese has oxidation state +2. The change in oxidation state is +7 to +2, a gain of 5 electrons per manganese atom. The half-reaction is: MnO4– + 8H+ + 5e– → Mn2+ + 4H2O. Therefore, the reduction of 1 mole of MnO4– to Mn2+ requires 5 moles of electrons, which corresponds to 5 Faradays (5F) of electric charge. One Faraday is the charge carried by 1 mole of electrons (96500 C mol–1).

questions.text: ऐल्कोहॉलों को सांद्र H2SO4 के साथ गर्म करने पर ऐल्कीन बनती हैं। अभिक्रिया का प्रथम चरण है :
questions.text_english: Alkenes are formed by heating alcohols with conc. H2SO4. The first step in the reaction is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) protonation of alcohol molecule. The acid-catalysed dehydration of alcohols to alkenes proceeds by an E1 mechanism in three steps. The first step is the protonation of the hydroxyl group of the alcohol by the strong acid (H2SO4), converting –OH into a good leaving group –OH2+. In the second step, the protonated alcohol loses water to form a carbocation. In the third step, a proton is lost from the adjacent carbon to give the alkene. Therefore, protonation of the alcohol is the very first step, before carbocation formation or water elimination.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जलीय NaCl का वैद्युत-अपघटन कैथोड पर H2 और ऐनोड पर Cl2 देता है।
कारण (R) : H2O की अपेक्षा क्लोरीन का ऑक्सीकरण विभव उच्चतर होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Electrolysis of aqueous NaCl gives H2 at cathode and Cl2 at anode.
Reason (R) : Chlorine has higher oxidation potential than H2O.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए कोडों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes given below.

options.A: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं और कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या करता है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) और कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परन्तु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) ग़लत है, परन्तु कारण (R) सही है।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The Assertion is true: during electrolysis of aqueous NaCl (brine), at the cathode H2O is preferentially reduced over Na+ (because Na+ reduction requires much more negative potential), giving H2 gas; at the anode Cl– is preferentially oxidised over OH– (despite its lower reduction potential) due to the high concentration of Cl– and the phenomenon of overpotential, giving Cl2 gas. The Reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion: Cl– has a higher tendency to get oxidised (higher oxidation potential) compared to H2O/OH–, which is precisely why Cl2 is produced at the anode rather than O2.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : क्यूप्रस लवण प्रतिचुम्बकीय होते हैं।
कारण (R) : क्यूप्रस आयन में पूर्ण भरित 3d-कक्षक होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Cuprous salts are diamagnetic.
Reason (R) : Cuprous ion has completely filled 3d-orbitals.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए कोडों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes given below.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). Cuprous ion is Cu+. Copper (Z=29) has configuration [Ar]3d104s1. When it loses one electron to form Cu+, its configuration becomes [Ar]3d10 — all ten 3d electrons are paired, giving fully filled 3d orbitals. Since there are no unpaired electrons, cuprous salts are diamagnetic. The Reason is correct (Cu+ has completely filled 3d10 configuration) and it is precisely the correct explanation for why Cu+ salts are diamagnetic — the absence of unpaired electrons means no net magnetic moment.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : n-ब्यूटिल ब्रोमाइड की तुलना में n-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड का क्वथनांक उच्चतर होता है।
कारण (R) : C–Br आबंध की तुलना में C–Cl आबंध अधिक ध्रुवीय होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : n-Butyl chloride has higher boiling point than n-Butyl bromide.
Reason (R) : C–Cl bond is more polar than C–Br bond.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए कोडों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes given below.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D). The Assertion is FALSE: n-butyl bromide actually has a HIGHER boiling point than n-butyl chloride, not lower. n-BuBr boils at about 101°C whereas n-BuCl boils at about 78°C. Boiling point of haloalkanes increases down the halogen group (Cl < Br < I) because the larger, more polarisable halogen atoms form stronger London dispersion (van der Waals) forces, requiring more energy to vaporise. The Reason is TRUE: C–Cl bond is indeed more polar than C–Br bond because chlorine is more electronegative than bromine. However, polarity is not what determines the boiling point difference here — it is the molecular mass and van der Waals forces. So Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : ऐनिलीन की तुलना में ऐसीटेनिलाइड कम क्षारकीय है।
कारण (R) : ऐनिलीन के ऐसीटिलीकरण के परिणामस्वरूप नाइट्रोजन पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व घटता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Acetanilide is less basic than aniline.
Reason (R) : Acetylation of aniline results in decrease of electron density on nitrogen.
questions.instruction_line: नीचे दिए गए कोडों में से सही उत्तर चुनिए।
questions.instruction_line_english: Select the correct answer from codes given below.

options.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
options_english.D: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A). The Assertion is true: acetanilide (C6H5NHCOCH3) is less basic than aniline (C6H5NH2). The Reason is also true and correctly explains the assertion. In aniline, the lone pair on nitrogen can be donated to a proton (basic behaviour), though it is already delocalised into the benzene ring. When aniline is acetylated to form acetanilide, the lone pair on nitrogen is now delocalised not only into the benzene ring but also into the carbonyl group (C=O) of the acetyl group through resonance. This further reduces the electron density on nitrogen, making the lone pair even less available for donation to a proton. Hence acetanilide is less basic than aniline, and the reason correctly accounts for this.

questions.text:
(क) किसी अभिकारक 'A' का अपघटन होता है। 'A' की सांद्रता की माप निश्चित अंतराल पर की गई जिसे नीचे दी गई सारणी में अंकित किया गया:
समय/घंटे | [A]/M
0 | 0.40
1 | 0.20
2 | 0.10
3 | 0.05
ऊपर दिए गए आंकड़ों के आधार पर, अभिक्रिया की कोटि की प्रागुक्ति कीजिए और इसके वेग नियम का व्यंजक लिखिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Reactant 'A' underwent a decomposition reaction. The concentration of 'A' was measured periodically and recorded in the table given below:
Time/Hours | [A]/M
0 | 0.40
1 | 0.20
2 | 0.10
3 | 0.05
Based on the above data, predict the order of the reaction and write the expression for the rate law.

OR

(b) The reaction between H2(g) and I2(g) was carried out in a sealed isothermal container. The rate law for the reaction was found to be:
Rate = k[H2][I2]
If 1 mole of H2(g) was added to the reaction chamber and the temperature was kept constant, then predict the change in rate of the reaction and the rate constant.

key_points: The concentration halves every hour: 0.40 → 0.20 → 0.10 → 0.05, indicating a constant half-life of 1 hour
Constant half-life is the characteristic of a first-order reaction
The reaction is first order; Rate law: Rate = k[A]
For OR part: Adding more H2 increases [H2], so the rate increases (rate = k[H2][I2]); the rate constant k remains unchanged since temperature is constant

questions.solution: Part (a): From the data, [A] decreases as follows: at t=0, [A]=0.40 M; at t=1 h, [A]=0.20 M; at t=2 h, [A]=0.10 M; at t=3 h, [A]=0.05 M. The concentration is exactly halved in every successive hour, giving a constant half-life (t1/2) of 1 hour. A constant half-life is the defining characteristic of a first-order reaction. Therefore, the reaction is first order. The rate law expression is: Rate = k[A]. Part (b) OR: The rate law is Rate = k[H2][I2]. Since temperature is kept constant, the rate constant k does not change (k depends only on temperature). However, adding 1 mole of H2 increases the concentration [H2] in the chamber. Since rate = k[H2][I2], an increase in [H2] will increase the rate of the reaction proportionally. The rate constant remains unchanged.
questions.topic: Order of Reaction and Rate Law

questions.text: PtCl4·2KCl, AgNO3 विलयन के साथ AgCl का अवक्षेप नहीं देता है। संकुल का संरचनात्मक सूत्र और IUPAC नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english: PtCl4·2KCl doesn't give precipitate of AgCl with AgNO3 solution. Write the structural formula and IUPAC name of the complex.

key_points: Since no AgCl precipitate forms, all Cl– ions are inside the coordination sphere (not free ionic Cl–)
Structural formula: K2[PtCl6]
IUPAC name: Potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV)

questions.solution: Since PtCl4·2KCl does not give a precipitate of AgCl with AgNO3 solution, it means there are no free Cl– ions in the solution. All four Cl– ions must be present inside the coordination sphere of platinum, not as counter ions. The two K+ ions act as counter cations. Therefore, the structural (coordination) formula is K2[PtCl6]. In this complex, Pt is in the +4 oxidation state and is coordinated to six Cl– ligands (four from PtCl4 and two from 2KCl), giving an octahedral complex anion [PtCl6]2–. The IUPAC name is Potassium hexachloridoplatinate(IV).

questions.text: ईंधन सेल को परिभाषित कीजिए। साधारण सेल की तुलना में ईंधन सेल के दो लाभ दीजिए।
questions.text_english: Define fuel cell. Give two advantages of fuel cell over ordinary cell.

key_points: A fuel cell is an electrochemical cell that converts the chemical energy of a fuel (like H2) directly into electrical energy through electrochemical oxidation
Advantage 1: High efficiency — fuel cells convert chemical energy directly to electrical energy without combustion, achieving higher efficiency (up to 70-75%) than ordinary cells or heat engines

Advantage 2: Continuous operation / non-polluting — fuel cells can operate continuously as long as fuel is supplied and produce water as a by-product (in H2-O2 fuel cell), making them environment-friendly

questions.solution: A fuel cell is a galvanic cell in which the energy produced by the combustion of fuels such as hydrogen, methane, methanol, etc. is directly converted into electrical energy. In a hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, H2 and O2 are continuously fed into the cell and electricity is produced along with water as the only by-product. Compared to ordinary cells, fuel cells offer two important advantages: first, they have much higher energy conversion efficiency (about 70%) because they bypass the thermodynamic limitations of heat engines and convert chemical energy directly to electrical energy; second, they are environmentally clean since the only product is water, unlike ordinary batteries that contain toxic heavy metals and electrolytes that create disposal problems.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं के मुख्य उत्पादों की संरचनाएं लिखिए:
(क) [साइक्लोहेक्सेनोन से जुड़ी CH2CH2–C(=O)–O–CH3 को NaBH4 के साथ]
(ख) 6CH3–C(CH3)(OH)–CH3 + 2Al →
questions.text_english:
Write the structures of the main products of the following reactions:
(a) Cyclohexanone ring with CH2CH2–C(=O)–O–CH3 side chain treated with NaBH4
(b) 6CH3–C(CH3)(OH)–CH3 + 2Al →

key_points: Part (a): NaBH4 is a mild reducing agent that selectively reduces ketones/aldehydes but NOT esters. The ketone (C=O) of cyclohexanone ring is reduced to a secondary alcohol (–OH), while the ester group (–C(=O)–O–CH3) remains unchanged. Product: the cyclohexanol ring with the –CH2CH2–COOCH3 side chain intact.
Part (b): 2-methyl-2-propanol (tert-butanol) reacts with aluminium. Product: Aluminium tert-butoxide, Al(OC(CH3)3)3, i.e., Al[OC(CH3)3]3 + 3/2 H2

questions.solution: Part (a): NaBH4 is a selective reducing agent that reduces only the carbonyl group of aldehydes and ketones; it does not reduce ester groups. In the given compound, the cyclohexanone (cyclic ketone) group is reduced to give a cyclohexanol ring, while the methyl ester (–COOCH3) side chain remains intact. The product is 1-(2-(methoxycarbonyl)ethyl)cyclohexan-1-ol. Part (b): tert-Butanol (2-methylpropan-2-ol) reacts with aluminium metal. The product is aluminium tert-butoxide, Al(OC(CH3)3)3, along with hydrogen gas (H2). The overall reaction is: 6 (CH3)3COH + 2Al → 2Al[OC(CH3)3]3 + 3H2.

questions.text: आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्लों से क्या अभिप्राय है? ऐमीनो अम्ल उभयधर्मी प्रकृति के क्यों होते हैं?
questions.text_english: What is meant by essential amino acids? Why are amino acids amphoteric in nature?

key_points: Essential amino acids are those that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained through diet
Examples include valine, leucine, lysine, methionine, threonine, tryptophan, phenylalanine, isoleucine

Amino acids are amphoteric because they contain both an acidic group (–COOH) and a basic group (–NH2) in the same molecule; the –COOH can donate a proton (act as acid) and –NH2 can accept a proton (act as base)

questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that are necessary for the normal growth and functioning of the human body but cannot be synthesised by the body itself. They must therefore be supplied through the diet. Examples include valine, leucine, isoleucine, lysine, methionine, threonine, tryptophan and phenylalanine. Amino acids are amphoteric in nature because each amino acid molecule contains both an acidic carboxyl group (–COOH) and a basic amino group (–NH2). The –COOH group can donate a proton and act as an acid, while the –NH2 group can accept a proton and act as a base. In aqueous solution, the –COOH donates a proton to –NH2, forming a zwitterion (+H3N–CHR–COO–), which can react with both acids and bases.

questions.text:
(क) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए:
(i) n-प्रोपिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में ऐलिल क्लोराइड अधिक तीव्रता से जल-अपघटित होता है।
(ii) ऐल्किल हैलाइडों को जब सिल्वर सायनाइड के साथ अभिक्रियित किया जाता है तब आइसोसायनाइड बनते हैं।
(iii) SN2 अभिक्रिया में t-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में मेथिल क्लोराइड OH– आयन के साथ अधिक शीघ्रता से अभिक्रिया करता है।
questions.text_english:
(a) Account for the following:
(i) Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride.
(ii) Isocyanides are formed when alkyl halides are treated with silver cyanide.
(iii) Methyl chloride reacts faster with OH– ion in SN2 reaction than t-butyl chloride.

OR

(b) Complete the following reactions by writing the structural formulae of 'A' and 'B':
(i) CH3CH=CH2 → (HBr/Peroxide) → A → (aq. KOH) → B
(ii) CH3CH2CHCH3|Cl → (alc. KOH, heat) → A → (HBr) → B
(iii) A → (Mg) → CH3CH2MgCl → (H2O/H+) → B (Main product)

key_points: (i) Allyl chloride (CH2=CH–CH2Cl) forms an allylic carbocation intermediate stabilised by resonance, making hydrolysis faster than n-propyl chloride which forms an unstabilised primary carbocation
(ii) AgCN is a covalent compound; the free carbon end of CN– attacks the alkyl halide (C-attack), giving isocyanide R–NC rather than nitrile R–CN

(iii) In SN2, the nucleophile attacks from the back; methyl chloride (CH3Cl) has no bulky substituents so the backside attack is unhindered; t-butyl chloride has three bulky methyl groups creating steric hindrance, greatly slowing SN2

questions.solution:
Part (a): (i) Allyl chloride (CH2=CHCH2Cl) undergoes hydrolysis faster than n-propyl chloride because the intermediate allylic carbocation (CH2=CH–CH2+) formed during ionisation is stabilised by resonance over two carbon atoms. The n-propyl carbocation has no such resonance stabilisation. (ii) Silver cyanide (AgCN) is a covalent compound in which the silver is bonded to nitrogen, making the carbon end of the ambident CN– nucleophile free to attack the alkyl halide. Since carbon attacks, the product is an isocyanide (R–N≡C:), not a nitrile. (iii) SN2 reaction requires backside attack by the nucleophile. Methyl chloride (CH3Cl) has only three hydrogen atoms attached to the carbon bearing Cl, offering no steric hindrance to the incoming OH– ion. t-Butyl chloride has three bulky methyl groups surrounding the reaction centre, causing severe steric hindrance and thus greatly retarding the SN2 pathway.

Part (b) OR: (i) A = CH3CH2CH2Br (1-bromopropane, anti-Markovnikov addition due to peroxide), B = CH3CH2CH2OH (1-propanol, from SN2 with aq. KOH). (ii) A = CH3CH2CH=CH2 (but-1-ene, elimination by alc. KOH), B = CH3CH2CHBrCH3 (2-bromobutane, Markovnikov addition of HBr). (iii) A = CH3CH2Cl (chloroethane, since Mg gives CH3CH2MgCl), B = CH3CH2CH2CH2OH... actually B = CH3CH2H = ethane... The Grignard reagent CH3CH2MgCl treated with H2O/H+ gives ethane (CH3CH3) as the main product. So A = CH3CH2Cl, B = CH3CH3.

questions.text:
25°C पर निम्नलिखित अर्ध-सेलों को जोड़कर बने वोल्टीय सेल का सेल विभव परिकलित कीजिए:
Al/Al3+ (0.001 M) तथा Ni/Ni2+ (0.1 M)
दिया गया है: E°Ni2+/Ni = –0.25 V, E°Al3+/Al = –1.66 V
questions.text_english:
Calculate the cell voltage of the voltaic cell which is set up by joining following half-cells at 25°C:
Al/Al3+ (0.001 M) and Ni/Ni2+ (0.1 M)
Given: E°(Ni2+/Ni) = –0.25 V, E°(Al3+/Al) = –1.66 V

key_points: Al is anode (more negative E°), Ni is cathode
E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.25 – (–1.66) = 1.41 V
Cell reaction: 2Al + 3Ni2+ → 2Al3+ + 3Ni, n = 6
Apply Nernst equation: Ecell = 1.41 – (0.0591/6) log ([Al3+]2/[Ni2+]3)

questions.solution: Al has E° = –1.66 V and Ni has E° = –0.25 V. Since Al has the more negative (lower) standard electrode potential, it acts as the anode (oxidation) and Ni acts as the cathode (reduction). The cell reaction is: 2Al(s) + 3Ni2+(aq) → 2Al3+(aq) + 3Ni(s). Number of electrons transferred, n = 6. E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = –0.25 – (–1.66) = +1.41 V. Using the Nernst equation: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0591/n) × log([Al3+]2/[Ni2+]3) = 1.41 – (0.0591/6) × log[(0.001)2/(0.1)3] = 1.41 – (0.00985) × log(10–6/10–3) = 1.41 – (0.00985) × log(10–3) = 1.41 – (0.00985)(–3) = 1.41 + 0.02955 ≈ 1.44 V.

questions.text:
निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक प्रेक्षण के लिए स्पष्टीकरण दीजिए:
(क) Mn3+ आयन ऑक्सीकारक है जबकि Cr2+ आयन अपचायक है यद्यपि दोनों का d-कक्षक विन्यास (d4) एक समान है।
(ख) लैंथेनॉयड आकुंचन की तुलना में एक तत्व से दूसरे तत्व के बीच ऐक्टिनॉयड आकुंचन अधिक होता है।
(ग) H, B, C और N के साथ संक्रमण धातुएं बहुत अधिक संख्या में अंतराकाशी यौगिक बनाती हैं।
questions.text_english:
Give explanation for each of the following observations:
(a) With the same d-orbital configuration (d4), Mn3+ ion is an oxidising agent whereas Cr2+ ion is a reducing agent.
(b) Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than that among lanthanoids.
(c) Transition metals form large number of interstitial compounds with H, B, C and N.

key_points: (a) Mn3+ (d4) tends to gain an electron to become Mn2+ (d5, half-filled, extra stable) — so it acts as oxidising agent; Cr2+ (d4) tends to lose an electron to become Cr3+ (d3, stable) — so it acts as reducing agent
(b) In actinoids, 5f orbitals are more diffuse and have poorer shielding than 4f orbitals of lanthanoids, so the effective nuclear charge increases more per element, causing greater contraction
(c) Transition metals have small atomic radii with large interstitial spaces in their crystal lattices; H, B, C, N atoms are small enough to fit into these spaces, forming interstitial compounds

questions.solution: Part (a): Although both Mn3+ and Cr2+ have d4 configuration, their behaviour differs due to the stability of neighbouring oxidation states. Mn3+ easily accepts an electron to form Mn2+ (d5 — half-filled, which is extra stable), so Mn3+ acts as an oxidising agent. Cr2+, on the other hand, easily loses an electron to form Cr3+ (d3 configuration, which is relatively stable), so Cr2+ acts as a reducing agent. Part (b): In actinoids, the 5f orbitals are more diffuse and have poorer shielding ability compared to the 4f orbitals in lanthanoids. As a result, the effective nuclear charge experienced by the outer electrons increases more significantly from one actinoid element to the next, leading to greater contraction per element than in lanthanoids. Part (c): Transition metals have compact crystal structures with small interstitial voids in their lattices. H, B, C, and N are small atoms that can fit into these interstitial spaces without breaking the original metallic structure. The transition metals' partially filled d-orbitals can form bonds with these small atoms, resulting in a large number of interstitial compounds.
questions.topic: Properties of Transition and Inner Transition Elements

questions.text:
NaOH का एक जलीय विलयन बनाया गया और परासरण दाब की माप से 27°C पर इसका मोलर द्रव्यमान 25 g mol–1 पाया गया। इस विलयन में NaOH का प्रतिशत वियोजन परिकलित कीजिए।
[परमाणु द्रव्यमान : Na = 23 u, O = 16 u, H = 1 u]
questions.text_english:
An aqueous solution of NaOH was made and its molar mass from the measurement of osmotic pressure at 27°C was found to be 25 g mol–1. Calculate the percentage dissociation of NaOH in this solution.
[Atomic mass : Na = 23 u, O = 16 u, H = 1 u]

key_points: Molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g/mol
Observed molar mass = 25 g/mol (lower due to dissociation)
van't Hoff factor i = Molar mass (theoretical) / Molar mass (observed) = 40/25 = 1.6
NaOH → Na+ + OH–, total particles = 1 + alpha + alpha = 1 + alpha per formula unit; i = 1 + alpha
1.6 = 1 + alpha → alpha = 0.6, percentage dissociation = 60%

questions.solution: The molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol–1. The observed molar mass from osmotic pressure measurement = 25 g mol–1. Since the observed molar mass is less than the theoretical value, NaOH has dissociated. The van't Hoff factor i = (theoretical molar mass)/(observed molar mass) = 40/25 = 1.6. NaOH dissociates as: NaOH → Na+ + OH–. If alpha is the degree of dissociation, then from 1 mole of NaOH, total moles of particles in solution = (1 – alpha) + alpha + alpha = 1 + alpha. Therefore, i = 1 + alpha = 1.6, which gives alpha = 0.6. The percentage dissociation of NaOH = 0.6 × 100 = 60%.
questions.topic: Colligative Properties and van't Hoff Factor

questions.text:
पूछे गए अनुसार निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को व्यवस्थित कीजिए:
(क) C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5NHCH3, C6H5NH2 — pKb मानों के घटते हुए क्रम में
(ख) C2H5OH, C2H5NH2, (CH3)2NH — क्वथनांक के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में
(ग) C6H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2 — जल में विलेयता के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में
questions.text_english:
Arrange the following compounds as asked:
(a) in decreasing order of pKb values: C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5NHCH3, C6H5NH2
(b) increasing order of boiling point: C2H5OH, C2H5NH2, (CH3)2NH
(c) increasing order of solubility in water: C6H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2

key_points: (a) Decreasing pKb (least basic first): C6H5NH2 > C6H5NHCH3 > C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)2NH
(b) Increasing boiling point: (CH3)2NH < C2H5NH2 < C2H5OH
(c) Increasing water solubility: C6H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH < C2H5NH2

questions.solution: Part (a): Higher pKb means weaker base (less basic). Aromatic amines are weaker bases than aliphatic amines because the lone pair on N is delocalised into the benzene ring. N-methylaniline (C6H5NHCH3) is slightly more basic than aniline because the methyl group donates electrons. Among aliphatic amines, secondary amine (C2H5)2NH is more basic than primary C2H5NH2 in aqueous solution due to greater inductive effect and solvation. Decreasing order of pKb: C6H5NH2 > C6H5NHCH3 > C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)2NH. Part (b): (CH3)2NH is a secondary amine with two N–H bonds; C2H5NH2 is a primary amine with two N–H bonds but slightly higher molecular mass; C2H5OH forms stronger hydrogen bonds (O–H···O) than N–H···N bonds. Increasing boiling point order: (CH3)2NH < C2H5NH2 < C2H5OH. Part (c): All three can form hydrogen bonds with water, but aryl amines are less soluble due to the hydrophobic benzene ring. Among aliphatic amines, (C2H5)2NH has a larger non-polar portion. Increasing solubility: C6H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH < C2H5NH2.

questions.text: C8H8O आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई ऐरोमैटिक यौगिक 'A' धनात्मक 2,4-DNP परीक्षण देता है। यह सोडियम हाइपोआयोडाइट के साथ अभिक्रियित किए जाने पर यौगिक 'B' का पीला अवक्षेप देता है। यौगिक 'A' टॉलेन अथवा फेलिंग अभिकर्मक के साथ अभिक्रिया नहीं करता है; KMnO4 के साथ प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण पर यह कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल 'C' बनाता है। 'A', 'B' और 'C' की संरचनाएं स्पष्ट कीजिए। उनके IUPAC नाम भी दीजिए।
questions.text_english: An aromatic compound 'A' with molecular formula C8H8O gives positive 2,4-DNP test. It gives yellow precipitate of compound 'B' on treatment with sodium hypoiodite. Compound 'A' does not react with Tollen's or Fehling's reagent; on drastic oxidation with KMnO4 it forms a carboxylic acid 'C'. Elucidate the structures of A, B and C. Also give their IUPAC names.

key_points: A gives 2,4-DNP test → has carbonyl group (ketone or aldehyde); does NOT react with Tollens/Fehling → NOT an aldehyde → must be a ketone
A gives iodoform test (yellow precipitate with NaOI) → has CH3CO– group (methyl ketone)
Molecular formula C8H8O; aromatic; methyl ketone; oxidation gives carboxylic acid → A = C6H5COCH3 (acetophenone/methyl phenyl ketone)
B = CHI3 (iodoform), yellow precipitate
C = C6H5COOH (benzoic acid)

questions.solution: The molecular formula C8H8O with degree of unsaturation = (2×8+2–8)/2 = 5, indicating an aromatic ring plus one more degree of unsaturation (C=O). The positive 2,4-DNP test confirms the presence of a carbonyl group (ketone or aldehyde). Since 'A' does not react with Tollens' or Fehling's reagents, it is not an aldehyde but a ketone. The positive iodoform test (yellow precipitate of CHI3 with sodium hypoiodite) confirms the presence of a methyl ketone (–COCH3) group. With the molecular formula C8H8O and an aromatic ring, compound A is acetophenone (methyl phenyl ketone), C6H5COCH3. IUPAC name of A: 1-phenylethan-1-one. On treatment with NaOI (sodium hypoiodite), the –COCH3 group gives iodoform: compound B = CHI3 (iodoform). IUPAC name of B: triiodomethane. On drastic oxidation with KMnO4, the methyl group attached to the ring is oxidised to give benzoic acid: compound C = C6H5COOH. IUPAC name of C: benzoic acid.
questions.topic: Chemical Tests for Aldehydes and Ketones

questions.text:
(क) क्या तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल एथिल ईथर बनाने के लिए सोडियम एथॉक्साइड और तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड का उपयोग किया जा सकता है? उचित व्याख्या दीजिए। तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल एथिल ईथर बनाने के लिए आवश्यक उपयुक्त प्रारम्भिक पदार्थों का सुझाव देते हुए अपने उत्तर का औचित्य दीजिए।
(ख) ऊपर उल्लिखित ईथर का IUPAC नाम दीजिए।
questions.text_english:
(a) Can sodium ethoxide and t-butyl chloride be used for the preparation of t-butyl ethyl ether? Give suitable explanation. Justify your answer by suggesting the appropriate starting material required for preparation of t-butyl ethyl ether.
(b) Give the IUPAC name of above mentioned ether.

key_points: No, sodium ethoxide and t-butyl chloride cannot be used — t-butyl chloride is a tertiary alkyl halide which undergoes elimination (E2) rather than SN2 with strong base/nucleophile like C2H5O–Na+, giving isobutylene instead of the ether
Correct method: Use sodium t-butoxide and ethyl chloride (primary alkyl halide) — primary alkyl halides undergo SN2 readily; (CH3)3CONa + C2H5Cl → (CH3)3C–O–C2H5 + NaCl
IUPAC name: 2-ethoxy-2-methylpropane

questions.solution: Part (a): No, sodium ethoxide (C2H5ONa) and t-butyl chloride ((CH3)3CCl) cannot be used to prepare t-butyl ethyl ether. t-Butyl chloride is a tertiary alkyl halide, and when treated with a strong base/nucleophile like sodium ethoxide (which is both a strong nucleophile and a strong base), the reaction predominantly follows the E2 elimination pathway rather than SN2 substitution. This is because the three bulky methyl groups on the t-butyl carbon create severe steric hindrance, preventing backside attack of the nucleophile. As a result, isobutylene (2-methylpropene) is the major product, not the ether. The correct approach for preparing t-butyl ethyl ether is to use sodium t-butoxide ((CH3)3CONa) with ethyl chloride (C2H5Cl, a primary alkyl halide): (CH3)3CONa + C2H5Cl → (CH3)3C–O–C2H5 + NaCl. Primary alkyl halides undergo SN2 readily without significant elimination. Part (b): The IUPAC name of t-butyl ethyl ether [(CH3)3C–O–C2H5] is 2-ethoxy-2-methylpropane.

questions.text: आदर्श विलयन की सामान्यत: स्वीकृत परिभाषा के अनुसार उसी अथवा भिन्न स्पीशीज़ के अणुओं के मध्य समान अन्योन्यक्रिया बल कार्य करते हैं। (यह कथन तुल्य है कि घटकों की सक्रियता उनकी सांद्रता के बराबर होती है।) सच पूछिए तो यह शर्त मिश्रणों (ध्रुवण समावयव, तत्व के समस्थानिक मिश्रणों, हाइड्रोकार्बन मिश्रणों) के लिए केवल अपवादात्मक प्रकरणों में ही पूरी होती है। आदर्श विलयनों के विषय में सीमित प्रकरणों में ही चर्चा की जा सकती है क्योंकि विलायक के संदर्भ में अत्यंत तनु विलयन ही आदर्शत: व्यवहार करते हैं। इस दृष्टिकोण को इस तथ्य से और भी समर्थन मिला कि राउल्ट नियम ने तनु विलयनों में विलायक के व्यवहार का वर्णन करने के लिए आनुभविक रूप से ज्ञात किया तथा पूर्वधारणा के माध्यम से ऊष्मागतिकी द्वारा विलायक के आदर्श व्यवहार को निगमित किया जा सकता है।
questions.text_english: According to the generally accepted definition of the ideal solution there are equal interaction forces acting between molecules belonging to the same or different species. (This is equivalent to the statement that the activity of the components equals the concentration.) Strictly speaking, this condition is fulfilled only in exceptional cases for mixtures (optical isomers, isotopic mixtures of an element, hydrocarbon mixtures). It is still usual to talk about ideal solutions as limiting cases in reality since very dilute solutions behave ideally with respect to the solvent. This view is further supported by the fact that Raoult's law empirically found for describing the behaviour of the solvent in dilute solutions can be deduced thermodynamically via the assumption of ideal behaviour of the solvent.

sub_questions.text_english: Give one example of miscible liquid pair which shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. What is the reason for such deviation?

key_points: Example: acetone-chloroform; negative deviation because A-B interactions are stronger than A-A and B-B interactions, reducing vapour pressure below the ideal value

sub_questions.solution: An example of a miscible liquid pair showing negative deviation from Raoult's law is acetone–chloroform (propanone–trichloromethane). Negative deviation occurs when the vapour pressure of the solution is lower than that predicted by Raoult's law. The reason is that the intermolecular interactions between unlike molecules (A–B type) are stronger than those between like molecules (A–A and B–B type). In acetone–chloroform, a hydrogen bond forms between the carbonyl oxygen of acetone and the hydrogen of chloroform, which is stronger than the original interactions in pure components. This stronger attraction reduces the tendency of molecules to escape into the vapour phase, lowering the vapour pressure.

sub_questions.text_english:
(i) State Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components.
OR
(ii) Raoult's law is a special case of Henry's law. Comment.

key_points: (i) For a solution of two volatile liquids A and B: partial pressure of each component equals its mole fraction times its pure vapour pressure. pA = xA × p°A; pB = xB × p°B

(ii) Henry's law: p = KH × x; Raoult's law: p = p° × x. When the solvent is considered and KH = p°, Raoult's law is a special case of Henry's law where the Henry's constant equals the vapour pressure of the pure solvent

sub_questions.solution:
Part (b)(i): Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components states that for any component in a solution, the partial vapour pressure of that component over the solution is equal to the mole fraction of that component in the solution multiplied by its vapour pressure in the pure state at the same temperature. Mathematically: pA = xA × p°A and pB = xB × p°B, where pA and pB are partial pressures, xA and xB are mole fractions, and p°A and p°B are vapour pressures of pure components.

Part (b)(ii) OR: Henry's law states that the partial pressure of a gas above a solution is proportional to its mole fraction in solution: p = KH × x. Raoult's law states that the vapour pressure of a component over its solution equals p° × x. Comparing both, when the proportionality constant KH equals p° (the vapour pressure of the pure solvent), Raoult's law and Henry's law become identical. Since for an ideal dilute solution the solvent obeys Raoult's law and p° is a constant at given temperature, Raoult's law is indeed a special case of Henry's law where KH = p°.

Mono-, di- and tri-phosphate forms are important, as well as 3-5 cyclic monophosphates. Purines and pyrimidines form an important class of compounds with ribose and deoxyribose. sub_questions.text_english: What products would be formed when DNA is hydrolysed? How is DNA different from RNA with reference to a structure?

key_points: Hydrolysis of DNA gives: phosphoric acid, 2-deoxyribose sugar, and nitrogenous bases (adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine)
Structural difference: DNA contains deoxyribose sugar and thymine base; RNA contains ribose sugar and uracil base instead of thymine

sub_questions.solution: When DNA is hydrolysed, the products formed are: phosphoric acid (H3PO4), 2-deoxyribose sugar, and the four nitrogenous bases — adenine, guanine, cytosine, and thymine. Structurally, DNA differs from RNA in two key ways: first, DNA contains 2-deoxyribose as the sugar component whereas RNA contains ribose (which has an –OH group at the 2' position instead of –H); second, DNA contains thymine (5-methyluracil) as one of its pyrimidine bases, whereas RNA contains uracil (without the methyl group) in place of thymine.

sub_questions.text: न्यूक्लियोटाइड और न्यूक्लियोसाइड में अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए।

key_points: Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + sugar (no phosphate); Nucleotide = nitrogenous base + sugar + phosphate group

sub_questions.solution: A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) linked to a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) through an N-glycosidic bond. It does not contain a phosphate group. A nucleotide is a nucleoside with one or more phosphate groups attached to the 5'-hydroxyl of the sugar through a phosphoester bond. In other words, nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group. For example, adenosine is a nucleoside, while adenosine monophosphate (AMP) is a nucleotide.

sub_questions.solution:
Part (c)(i): Two important functions of nucleic acids are: first, DNA stores the genetic information of an organism in the sequence of its bases and transmits this hereditary information faithfully from one generation to the next during cell division; second, RNA (specifically mRNA) acts as a messenger, carrying the genetic code from DNA in the nucleus to the ribosomes in the cytoplasm, where it directs the synthesis of specific proteins (translation).

Part (c)(ii) OR: The linkage that joins two nucleotides together in a nucleic acid chain is the 3',5'-phosphodiester bond (phosphodiester linkage). This bond is formed between the 3'-OH of one nucleotide's sugar and the 5'-phosphate group of the next nucleotide. The nitrogenous base that is found in RNA but not in DNA is Uracil. In DNA, the corresponding base is Thymine (5-methyluracil), while RNA contains uracil in its place.

key_points: 31(a)(i)(I): Cyclohexanone + semicarbazide → cyclohexanone semicarbazone (C=N–NHCONH2)
31(a)(i)(II): (CH3)2Cd + 2CH3COCl → 2CH3COCH3 (acetone/propan-2-one) + CdCl2
31(a)(i)(III): Benzoyl chloride + H2/Pd-BaSO4 (Rosenmund reduction) → benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
31(a)(ii)(I): Add NaHCO3 — benzoic acid fizzes/dissolves (gives CO2); ethyl benzoate does not react
31(a)(ii)(II): Tollens test — propanal gives silver mirror; propanone does not; OR iodoform test — propanone (methyl ketone) gives yellow CHI3; propanal does not
31(b)(i)(I): Product = benzoic acid (C6H5COOH)
31(b)(i)(II): Reagent = O3 followed by Zn/H2O (ozonolysis) to give cyclohexanecarbaldehyde
31(b)(i)(III): Product — [Ag(NH3)2]+ (Tollens) oxidises the aldehyde group only; ketone unreacted; product = silver mirror + 4-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid salt
31(b)(ii)(I): PhCHO + PhMgBr → PhCH(OH)Ph → [O] → Ph-CO-Ph (benzophenone)
31(b)(ii)(II): PhCHO + CH2=PPh3 (Wittig) or Aldol approach: PhCHO + CH3CHO → PhCH=CHCHO → H2 → PhCH2CH2CH2OH

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): Reaction (I): Cyclohexanone reacts with semicarbazide (H2NCONHNH2) by nucleophilic addition-elimination to give cyclohexanone semicarbazone, in which the C=O of cyclohexanone is replaced by C=N–NH–CO–NH2. Reaction (II): Dimethylcadmium ((CH3)2Cd) reacts with acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) by the Cadmium reagent reaction to give acetone (CH3COCH3) and CdCl2 — this is a method to prepare symmetrical ketones using dialkylcadmium and acid chlorides. Reaction (III): Benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl) undergoes Rosenmund reduction (H2 over Pd-BaSO4 catalyst) to give benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO).

Part (a)(ii): Test (I): Add sodium bicarbonate solution (NaHCO3). Benzoic acid is a carboxylic acid and reacts with NaHCO3 to give brisk effervescence of CO2. Ethyl benzoate is an ester and does not react with NaHCO3, giving no effervescence. Test (II): Perform Tollens' test (add Tollens' reagent, [Ag(NH3)2]+). Propanal (an aldehyde) gives a silver mirror on the walls of the test tube. Propanone (a ketone) does not react with Tollens' reagent and gives no silver mirror.

Part (b)(i): Product (I): Ethylbenzene on treatment with KMnO4/KOH followed by acidification with H3O+ gives benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) — the side chain is oxidised to –COOH. Reagent (II): The conversion of cyclohexylidene methane (cyclohexane=CH2) to cyclohexane carbaldehyde involves ozonolysis (O3) followed by reductive workup (Zn/H2O), which cleaves the C=C double bond to give the aldehyde. Product (III): [Ag(NH3)2]+ (Tollens' reagent) selectively oxidises the aldehyde group (–CHO) to –COO– (carboxylate), giving a silver mirror. The ketone group (C=O on the ring) does not react. Product = silver mirror + ammonium salt of 4-oxocyclohexane-1-carboxylic acid.

Part (b)(ii): Conversion (I): Benzaldehyde to benzophenone — React benzaldehyde with phenyl magnesium bromide (PhMgBr, a Grignard reagent) to give benzhydrol (Ph2CHOH) after hydrolysis; then oxidise with an oxidising agent (like CrO3 or PCC) to get benzophenone (Ph2C=O). Conversion (II): Benzaldehyde to 3-phenyl propanol — React benzaldehyde with acetaldehyde in aldol condensation (NaOH) to give cinnamaldehyde (PhCH=CHCHO); then reduce the C=C and C=O bonds with H2/Ni (catalytic hydrogenation) to give 3-phenylpropan-1-ol (PhCH2CH2CH2OH).

questions.text_english:
(a) (i) Give reasons:
(I) [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic whereas [NiCl4]2– is paramagnetic. [Atomic number: Ni = 28]
(II) CO is a stronger complexing agent than NH3.
(III) The trans isomer of complex [Co(en)2Cl2]+ is optically inactive.
(ii) Using Crystal Field Theory, write the number of unpaired electrons in octahedral complexes of Fe3+ in the presence of:
(I) Strong field ligand
(II) Weak field ligand [Atomic number: Fe = 26]

OR

(b) (i) Name the type of isomerism exhibited by the following compounds. Also draw their corresponding isomers.
(I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6]
(II) [Co(en)3]3+
(III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3]
(ii) Differentiate between weak field and strong field ligands. How does the strength of the ligand influence the spin of the complex?

key_points: (a)(i)(I): In [Ni(CO)4], CO is a strong field ligand causing electron pairing; Ni is Ni(0) with d10 configuration — all electrons paired → diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]2–, Cl– is weak field; Ni2+ has d8 configuration with 2 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic
(a)(i)(II): CO acts as both a sigma donor and a pi acceptor (back-bonding from metal d-orbitals to CO empty pi* orbitals), making it a stronger ligand than NH3 which is only a sigma donor
(a)(i)(III): Trans-[Co(en)2Cl2]+ has a plane of symmetry (the plane containing Co, two Cl, and bisecting both en ligands), making it superimposable on its mirror image → optically inactive
(a)(ii)(I): Strong field: Fe3+ is d5; with strong field pairing occurs giving t2g5 eg0 → 1 unpaired electron
(a)(ii)(II): Weak field: Fe3+ d5; no pairing, t2g3 eg2 → 5 unpaired electrons

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i)(I): Nickel (Z=28) has configuration [Ar]3d84s2. In [Ni(CO)4], nickel is in zero oxidation state (Ni0) with configuration 3d10 (all electrons paired) because CO is a very strong field ligand that causes complete electron pairing. With no unpaired electrons, [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]2–, nickel is in +2 oxidation state (Ni2+) with configuration 3d8. Cl– is a weak field ligand, so no forced pairing occurs beyond what exists naturally in d8. In a tetrahedral weak field, Ni2+ has 2 unpaired electrons, making [NiCl4]2– paramagnetic.

Part (a)(i)(II): CO is a stronger complexing agent than NH3 because it is a pi-acceptor ligand in addition to being a sigma donor. CO donates a lone pair from carbon to the metal (sigma donation) and simultaneously accepts electron density from the filled metal d-orbitals back into its empty antibonding pi* orbitals (pi back-bonding or back-donation). This synergistic bonding — sigma donation + pi back-acceptance — greatly strengthens the metal-ligand bond. NH3 is only a sigma donor and cannot participate in back-bonding, making CO far superior as a complexing agent.

Part (a)(i)(III): The trans isomer of [Co(en)2Cl2]+ has the two Cl– ligands in trans positions (180° apart) and the two en ligands in the equatorial plane. This arrangement possesses a plane of symmetry: the plane containing the Co atom, both Cl atoms, and passing through the midpoints of the two en ligands. Because of this plane of symmetry, the molecule is superimposable on its mirror image and hence is optically inactive (achiral).

Part (a)(ii): Fe3+ has electronic configuration [Ar]3d5 — five d-electrons. In an octahedral crystal field with a strong field ligand (e.g., CN–), the crystal field splitting energy (CFSE, Delta) is large and greater than the pairing energy. All five electrons are forced into the lower t2g set: t2g5 eg0, giving only 1 unpaired electron (low spin complex). With a weak field ligand (e.g., F– or Cl–), Delta is small and less than the pairing energy. Electrons fill orbitals following Hund's rule: t2g3 eg2, giving 5 unpaired electrons (high spin complex).

Part (b)(i): (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows ionisation isomerism. The isomers are [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] and [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6] — exchange of ligands between the two coordination spheres. (II) [Co(en)3]3+ shows optical isomerism (enantiomers). The D (or Lambda) and L (or Delta) forms of the tris-chelate complex are non-superimposable mirror images. (III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] shows linkage isomerism (because NO2– is an ambident ligand — can coordinate through N as nitro or through O as nitrito) and also facial-meridional (fac-mer) geometrical isomerism.

Part (b)(ii): Weak field ligands (e.g., halides like F–, Cl–, Br–, I–, and H2O) cause a small crystal field splitting (small Delta). They cannot force electron pairing, so electrons fill all d-orbitals singly before pairing (following Hund's rule), resulting in high spin complexes with maximum unpaired electrons. Strong field ligands (e.g., CN–, CO, NO2–, en, NH3 in higher position) cause a large crystal field splitting (large Delta). When Delta exceeds the pairing energy, electrons pair up in the lower energy orbitals (t2g), resulting in low spin complexes with fewer unpaired electrons. Therefore, the strength of the ligand directly determines whether a complex is high spin or low spin.

N2O5(g) → 2NO2(g) + 1/2 O2(g)
was 1.2 × 10–2 mol L–1. The concentration of N2O5 after 60 minutes was 0.2 × 10–2 mol L–1. Calculate the rate constant of the reaction at 318 K.

(ii) Account for the following:

(b) (i) The rate of the chemical reaction doubles for an increase of 10 K in absolute temperature from 298 K. Calculate activation energy (Ea).
[2.303 R = 19.15 JK–1 mol–1, log 2 = 0.3]
(ii) For a reaction: 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2 (catalysed by I–), the proposed mechanism is:
(I) H2O2 + I– → H2O + IO– (slow)
(II) H2O2 + IO– → H2O + I– + O2 (fast)
(1) Write rate law for the reaction.
(2) Write the overall order and molecularity of the reaction.

key_points: (a)(ii)(I): The order of reaction depends on the actual mechanism (rate-determining step), not on stoichiometric coefficients in the balanced equation; elementary and complex reactions differ

(a)(ii)(II): If one reactant is in large excess (solvent-like conditions), its concentration remains essentially constant — the reaction becomes pseudo-first order (e.g., acid hydrolysis of ester in excess water)
(b)(i): Using Arrhenius equation log(k2/k1) = Ea/2.303R × (T2–T1)/(T1×T2); log 2 = Ea/(19.15) × 10/(298×308); Ea ≈ 52897 J/mol ≈ 52.9 kJ/mol

questions.solution:
Part (a)(i): For a first-order reaction, the rate constant is given by k = (2.303/t) × log([A]0/[A]t). Here [A]0 = 1.2 × 10–2 mol L–1, [A]t = 0.2 × 10–2 mol L–1, t = 60 min. k = (2.303/60) × log(1.2 × 10–2 / 0.2 × 10–2) = (2.303/60) × log 6 = (2.303/60) × 0.778 = 1.792/60 = 0.02987 min–1 ≈ 2.99 × 10–2 min–1.

Part (a)(ii)(I): The order of a reaction cannot be determined from the balanced chemical equation because the balanced equation tells us only about the stoichiometry of the overall reaction, not about the mechanism by which it proceeds. The rate law and order are determined experimentally and depend on the slowest (rate-determining) elementary step in the mechanism. A balanced equation often represents the net result of several elementary steps, and the order may be completely different from the stoichiometric coefficients.

Part (a)(ii)(II): A bimolecular reaction (Rate = k[A][B]) can behave as a first-order reaction if one of the reactants is present in such a large excess that its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. For example, in the acid hydrolysis of an ester in aqueous solution, water is present in such a large excess that its concentration does not change appreciably. The rate then depends only on the ester concentration: Rate = k'[ester], making it a pseudo-first-order reaction.

Part (b)(i): Using the Arrhenius equation in the form: log(k2/k1) = [Ea/2.303R] × [(T2 – T1)/(T1 × T2)]. Given: k2/k1 = 2 (rate doubles), T1 = 298 K, T2 = 308 K, T2 – T1 = 10 K, 2.303R = 19.15 J K–1 mol–1. log 2 = [Ea/19.15] × [10/(298 × 308)]. 0.3 = [Ea/19.15] × [10/91784]. Ea = 0.3 × 19.15 × 91784/10 = 0.3 × 19.15 × 9178.4 = 52,736 J mol–1 ≈ 52.7 kJ mol–1.

Part (b)(ii): The rate-determining (slow) step is: H2O2 + I– → H2O + IO–. The rate law is therefore written from this slow step: Rate = k[H2O2][I–]. The overall order of the reaction = 1 + 1 = 2 (second order). The molecularity of the rate-determining step = 2 (since two molecules, H2O2 and I–, participate in the slow step), so the molecularity is bimolecular.
